content: Lansoprazole reduces the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, which can lead to treatment failure or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs and is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by altering its metabolism through hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), including lansoprazole, with secretin may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during stimulation testing, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Discontinue lansoprazole at least 30 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to return to baseline. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If medically necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. The use of other PPIs with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir has not been studied. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after a locally-acting antacid. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Conversely, lansoprazole decreases the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, potentially reducing sparsentan exposure and efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur. Sucralfate decreases the levels of lansoprazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 30 minutes and monitor closely. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant administration may increase tacrolimus whole blood concentrations, particularly in intermediate or poor metabolizers of CYP2C19. Monitor closely. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. Conversely, tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, as it is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. Lansoprazole increases the levels of theophylline by decreasing its metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Prolonged use of PPIs can cause hypochlorhydria, which may alter gastrointestinal motility. Monitor for toxicity. Lansoprazole decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing gastric pH. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. Monitor closely. Lansoprazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Triclabendazole increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole use, recheck levels after discontinuation of triclabendazole. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, potentially reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor closely. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lansoprazole is used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as GERD, ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It works by reducing stomach acid production. Lansoprazole is available in delayed-release oral capsules (15 mg, 30 mg) and orally disintegrating tablets (15 mg, 30 mg). It should be stored at room temperature (68°F to 77°F) and protected from extreme temperatures. Common side effects include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. Serious side effects include acute interstitial nephritis, Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea, severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), lupus, vitamin B12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, and bone loss or fractures. Seek immediate medical attention if severe symptoms occur.
